summary: 1 John 4 (21 verses) continues the story of light, love, assurance. Starting with 'Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.', it moves through themes of light, love, assurance and calls readers toward light, love, assurance.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows light, love, assurance lived out in assurance against false teaching. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother.

questions.question: What is happening in 1 John 4?
questions.answer: In 21 verses, this chapter 1 john 4 (21 verses) continues the story of light, love, assurance. starting with 'beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of god, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.', it moves through themes of light, love, assurance and calls readers toward light, love, assurance. The setting is assurance against false teaching, written to churches. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote 1 John and why 4 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally john, addressed to churches around ad 85-95. This chapter fits the book's purpose as letter — its themes of light, love, assurance build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'prophet' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Messenger speaking for God. In this chapter, it appears in context of light, love, assurance. For a first-time reader: think of it as messenger speaking for god, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through light, love, assurance and faith, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 3 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'and every spirit who doesn’t confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that it comes. Now it i...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about light, love, assurance. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
